erica_eng: quick Q - I'm scheduled for a 6-week unpaid leave starting 2026-09-01. If I stop deferrals while I'm out, can I do a one-time "catch-up" contribution after I return to make up the missed deferrals?

nina_benefits: hey @erica_eng :wave: short answer: payroll can't backdate employee deferrals. Some vendors accept a one-time after-the-fact contribution if plan admin approves and it doesn't exceed IRS limits. Not guaranteed.

erica_eng: ok. timeline/ops wise, what's needed to attempt that?

 tom_payroll: payroll detail - deadline to change deferrals before a pay run is EOD two business days before payroll. For a post-return catch-up, we'd need: 1) written approval from benefits/plan admin; 2) signed vendor one-time contribution form; 3) payroll remittance or vendor ACH acceptance. Forus needs 5 business days to post once we send file.

forus-rep: Forus ops here - confirm we can process one-time contribution files with plan admin approval. Required fields: participant ID, amount, tax year. Send to transfers@forus.example. If amount would push you over the annual deferral limit, we'll reject.

erica_eng: got it. Also have an active 401k loan - if I'm unpaid, will repayments pause or do I have to set up ACH?

 tom_payroll: loan repayments are payroll-deducted by default. If no payroll, set up ACH with the vendor to keep payments current. Missed repayments can be treated as a distribution (taxable + possible 10% penalty if under 59\u00bd). DM me and I'll start ACH paperwork.

nina_benefits: next steps for @erica_eng: 1) DM me leave dates and if you want to request a catch-up (amount); 2) DM Tom for ACH if you want loan repayments while unpaid; 3) we'll confirm with Forus and update here.

benefits-bot: Doc: https://benefits.redwood.example/401k-faq (see "Leaves & Catch-up Contributions")

erica_eng: thanks everyone. I'll DM dates and the amount I want to request for the catch-up. :thanks:
